steps.text: Winter 1092
Border Battlefield, Kazdel

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Those rampaging cystybeasts... are they migrating? The vanguard never stood a chance. All those who didn't get out of the way in time were...

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: And those soldiers, moving in perfect coordination without exchanging a word... None of that was in the Intel!
That's not what we need to worry about.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: I'm the ranking officer now. All survivors, form up and retreat immediately. These supplies are crucial. It will be a hard winter without them.

steps.name: Composed Soldier
steps.text: Yes, ma'am. But how did things go so wrong even though we made our move early? Did our informant—

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: The intel was good. We were delayed by the mercenaries transporting the supplies. They upped the price on the spot. I've dealt with them.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: This is why I hate mercenaries.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Another coincidence...

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: It's not a coincidence if it keeps happening over and over again. We've had way too many setbacks lately.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: Focus, Babel forces must be—

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Wait, hel—
A flash of white, and a hole appears in the soldier's forehead. They cannot even tell where the attack is coming from, in the noise of the cystybeast stampede.

a.text: 'Leave the supplies behind, and you may leave unharmed. You have been warned.'

steps.text: Without warning, Ulšulah hears a cold, coarse voice in her head.

steps.name: Composed Soldier
steps.text: He... he's dead. *Sarkaz expletive* We need to withdraw! Did you hear that voice?

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: Hmph... just a bluff! Keep your head low and stay with me!

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: Don't get separated! Stick together, if you want to live! We need to get these supplies back!

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: As for the vanguard... we're in no position to think about them.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: They're retreating. I suppose nabbing the supplies isn't so easy after all.

a.text: 'Be patient and follow the Doctor's instructions. The Chairman has said that the priority is to minimize casualties.'

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: I know, Mantra.
Mantra's lips are closed, but Scout can hear her voice clearly in his head.
She is the perfect coordinator for Babel's covert operations, and a shadow that eats away at the enemy's sanity.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: The enemy vanguard has been scattered by the herd. The survivors have fled into the woods.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: The enemy's actions were spontaneous, unplanned. They must have known that we decrypted their communications. But the envelopment succeeded nonetheless.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: We can leave the rest to Ascalon.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: Ascalon will not fail.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: Neither will we.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: Hah, you're absolutely right. You should get some rest, Mantra. 'Talking' takes a toll on you.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: No need to worry about the follow-up. We have the Doctor.

steps.name: Dying Mercenary
steps.text: Who directed this operation... the evil spirit again? Just what is this commander? Which Royal Court does it come from?

spans.text: Who directed this operation... the evil spirit again? Just what
this commander? Which Royal Court does it come from?

steps.name: Dying Mercenary
steps.text: If it can do this to us, it can do it to you too! Why would you sell your soul to something like that?!

steps.name: Dying Mercenary
steps.text: I'm getting out of here alive—
The mercenary hears breathing in the darkness not far away and swings his sword without hesitation.

steps.name: Dying Mercenary
steps.text: Got you!

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Dying Mercenary
steps.text: You're wounded too. You think you could kill me and walk away alive?

steps.name: Dying Mercenary
steps.text: Get out of my way, or I'll kill you, if it's the last thing I do!

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: You're not taking Marcel's things. He's going home.

steps.name: Dying Mercenary
steps.text: Home? *cough* *cough*—

steps.name: Dying Mercenary
steps.text: Our home is... Kazdel! You— traitors to Kazdel...
The mercenary keeps swinging his sword at Odda, who only passively blocks with his hammer.
The mercenary's movement slows down, and his breathing grows weak.

steps.name: Dying Mercenary
steps.text: Babel... morons...

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: Wasn't it the Military Commission who betrayed Kazdel?

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Relax. He's dead.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Be more decisive next time, Odda, and there'll be fewer injuries.

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: The entire squad is dead... they should have died an honorable death, not tormented by fear—

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: This is not the right time to show mercy. Bring Marcel. Our mission is finished.

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: You... you remember his name?

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: I remember everyone in Babel, the living and the dead, the ones who had names, and the ones who didn't.

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: I could have saved him... it's just hard to raise your weapon against your own kin.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Even if it's to avenge Marcel?

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Your father died in the chaos of the city. Have you ever thought about seeking vengeance for him?
Odda takes a deep breath.

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: I hate the people who killed him, but vengeance doesn't change anything.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: A classical idea. Rational, righteous, human.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: What if your vendetta is with a cold-blooded deathmonger, with hands soaked in blood?

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Would you say you kill for justice and your ideals, without a hint of hatred?

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: I... I'm not sure.

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: Do you regret killing mercenaries who threaten Babel, Ascalon?

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: Then I won't either.

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: Even if it means I have to...

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: O-Oh, I'm sorry! I'm saying silly things again. Don't mind me, I'm not important at all—

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: No, all Babelites are important to Her Highness.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Time to go back.
Rhodes Island of Babel, Kazdel

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: What are you here for?

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: I've already said it many times. It was my own decision to betray Her Highness.

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: It had nothing to do with the Military Commission, and I'm not an informer for them.

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: You want to execute me, make it quick.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: I'm not here to torture you.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: I brought some wine.

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: I don't need it.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: Are you sure? This is Victorian fruit wine, not some lousy swill.

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: What are you here for?

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: To catch up about old times.

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: We have nothing to talk about.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: I know Scout's hiding something from me. Ascalon would too, because she knows we know each other.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: But I can make a pretty good guess why you wanted to kill the Doctor.

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: Be my guest.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: You're not a sore loser. You're unhappy because the Doctor is an outsider.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: Everyone wants Babel and the Military Commission to get along. You believe that Dr. Kal'tsit and the Doctor have widened the rift, rather than mended it.

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: Good guess. Now get out.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: I'm an outsider too. And I'm still fighting for the Sarkaz to this day.

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: You—

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: The wine.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: You're drinking out of your hat?

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: Do you see a wine glass in this cell? You should have brought one.

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: *gulp* — Ah.

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: What happened to the rest of your team?

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: Let's see... the one with the spear, the caster, the one with the shield who's sitting here right now, a medic, and a sniper?

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: Skullspear, White Smoke, Grey Sun, Stross, Walnut, Kung, Herb.

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: So the sniper's name was Herb.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: He's dead. Let bygones be bygones.

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: All good fighters.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: If I ever get to mentor the young, I'll raise them to be that kind of fighter.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: Selfless, honest, cautious about picking a side, but committed once they've made their choice.

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: Pah. How sentimental.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: Do the Sarkaz hate outsiders in Babel that much?

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: Fools like you who would give your lives for Her Highness wouldn't understand.

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: Babel might be changing certain things, but it's meaningless. It's not fast enough, and its reach is not far enough.

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: Her Highness did not have to have her hands tied. She didn't need to waste her time.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: The Doctor helped Chairman Theresa a lot.

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: In what capacity?

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: A researcher? A military commander?

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: Both.

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: Even though the Doctor killed so many Sarkaz? The more people like that, the longer the war will drag on.

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: Her Highness's achievements are grand. She's solved problems all her life, taken care of the needs of generations, and now she leads the fight against Oripathy.

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: But what's happening now? We're fighting the Military Commission. Fighting our own. That's not part of her vision.

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: Oh, I almost forgot. You're a mercenary, but you're not a Sarkaz mercenary.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: True enough.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: I only came to Babel because I was with the others. I got involved in this because most of my people were Sarkaz.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: Oh, White Smoke is dead, too.

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: Why bring her up now?

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: I thought maybe there was something going on between you two.

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: Doesn't matter. She's dead.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: She died in the presence of Chairman Theresa.

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: Damn, now I'm starting to envy her. What happened?

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: Ambush. Only the two of us survived, but she lost her legs to an Arts trap. I had to drag her through the mud.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: That's when we ran into Chairman Theresa. Well, we ran into the Doctor first.

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: Pah. The evil spirit showed up on the battlefield personally?

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: Believe it or not, I thought I was looking at a Lateran priest when I first saw the Doctor in the distance.

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: The Doctor was praying with that black hood bowed low, next to the glowing Chairman.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: Wasn't even kneeling or doing any sort of ritual, just gazing silently into the distance with Chairman Theresa.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: That evil spirit you're talking about, Dr. {@nickname}, is not some heartless monster.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: The Doctor is torn, wandering in solitude... and still, in the end, chose to bring victory to Babel.

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: So you came to preach? You're trying to guilt-trip me?!

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: Get out and take your bloody wine! Did you think I would—

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: No, you're not that naive.

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: Has a decision been made?

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: Death sentence?

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: The Doctor and Chairman Theresa had reservations, but Dr. Kal'tsit and most of the fighters who participated in the operation won't have it any other way.

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: What about you?

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: Your betrayal cost us dozens of lives, brother.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: This time, I'm with Dr. Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: Hmph. More wine.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: You just spilled the last of it.

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: Are you gonna be doing it?

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: Yes. No need to burden Scout. He's tough on the outside but tender inside. And I don't want to hand you over to anyone else.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: I came to tell you, brother, that even though you did something stupid...

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: Babel will remember your name. We'll keep fighting, keeping your warning and reproach in our hearts.

steps.name: Sarkaz Traitor
steps.text: Train some promising young ones while you still can. Decent ones like you don't live long.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: Guess so.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: See you again, when the Sarkaz can finally live in peace.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: The traitors and spies have been executed. Royal Court spies. They really have a lot of problems in their tribe.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Good work. What about the unit that entered the war zone?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Scouts report that they blocked key passages leading out of the mountains after attacking Babel positions.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: The General did not order this. Was it someone from a Royal Court... or a Siracusan plot?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Unlikely. Reports indicate no particular bloodline characteristics to the witchcraft, and little effort was made to cipher communications. It's a rabble.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: May I speak frankly, sir? The unit may be rogue, but they just happened to cram Babel in with the Catastrophe.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Isn't that a good thing for us?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: What about the other commanders and mercenary captains?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Watching the show, of course, waiting to see if the enemy chooses to surrender, or die at the hands of the Catastrophe and the ruffians.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: I wouldn't overthink it if I were you, sir.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: You've shown as much mercy as you possibly could by ordering that we pull out of the valley and leave an opening for them.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Who knows, maybe some of my family are in that Catastrophe. I've gotten over it.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: You don't care?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: I try not to.
Rhodes Island of Babel, Kazdel

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: Sorry I'm late.

steps.name: Pith
steps.text: No need to start from the beginning. Ace was called on short notice. Just follow Mantra's instructions.

steps.name: Pith
steps.text: Go ahead. We don't have much time.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: Emergency?

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: (Nods)

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: I'll keep going then.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: We have twenty five hundred souls in the Catastrophe radius, mostly medics, Infected civilians, prisoners, and injured mercenaries.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: The scale of the Catastrophe is larger than the Catastrophe Messengers predicted. It's currently expected to affect five outposts, three key passages, and a field hospital repurposed from an abandoned town.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: They had almost made it out of the Catastrophe radius when their path was cut off by mercenaries.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: Trapping medics, wounded and civilians to die in a Catastrophe?

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: Is Manfred willing to go to such lengths these days?

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: It's not his style. The three Military Commission units have retreated from the forest, even leaving a humanitarian corridor open in one of the canyons.

steps.name: Pith
steps.text: The Military Commission has casters on the cliffs, ready to annihilate any armed unit that attempts to pass through.

steps.name: Pith
steps.text: But they're not trying to hide what they're doing, and they're not doing anything we didn't expect.

steps.name: Pith
steps.text: These mercenaries are different. They came out of nowhere, attacked our positions, destroyed important roads and bridges, and polluted several water sources in the mountains with Originium explosives. There seems to be no reason with their actions.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: Who's their employer?

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: We're still looking into it, but based on what little intelligence we have, it's very likely that they're rogue.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: Revenge, a last-gasp struggle after being abandoned by Theresis, instigation by another country... anything's possible.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Doesn't matter. I'll find out who their leader is, and kill them.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Without leader, a band of aimless mercenaries is just a useless rabble.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: You go save those people. We'll regroup back at base.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: I'll leave them to you, then.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: One last message. Her Highness says this operation is not part of the 'campaign'.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: We should be relieved.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: In a war that has become increasingly gridlocked, the opposing sides have a chance to work together for a common goal...

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: Saving lives from Catastrophe.
